title: Storing scenarios and results in SQLite

questions.heading: Foreign Keys Are Off Until a Connection Turns Them On, Outside Any Transaction
questions.stem: A service opens its database with sqlite3.connect(path, autocommit=False), then runs PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON. Later it inserts a run that names a scenario id the scenario table does not have. What happens?

options.text: The run is stored, since the pragma ran inside an already open transaction
options.says: Right: the program printed foreign_keys=0 and 'orphan run stored'.

options.text: The run is refused, since the pragma switched foreign keys on for it
options.says: The program printed foreign_keys=0 for exactly this order: the pragma did nothing.

options.text: The run is refused, since the REFERENCES clause is checked by the schema
options.says: SQLite's foreign key enforcement is off by default and switched on per connection.

options.text: The insert raises an error, since the pragma failed when it was sent
options.says: The pragma does nothing and reports no error; the orphan run was stored.

questions.heading: A Change and Its Audit Entry Commit Together, or Not at All
questions.stem: Inside one 'with conn:' block, the store inserts a run row and then its plan rows; the third plan row breaks a NOT NULL rule and raises. What does the database hold for that run afterwards?

options.text: The run row alone, since the block undoes just the statement that failed
options.says: The context manager rolls back the whole block when it raises; runs stayed at 2.

options.text: The run row and two plan rows, since each insert commits as it runs
options.says: Nothing commits until the block ends normally; the run count stayed at 2.

options.text: No row of that run, since the block's earlier inserts are rolled back too
options.says: Right: the program counted two runs before and after the failed save.

options.text: The run and its plan rows, with the third row's year stored as NULL
options.says: NOT NULL refused that row with IntegrityError, and the run count stayed at 2.

questions.heading: The Database Refuses What No Caller May Do
questions.stem: A maintenance script connects to the store directly and runs UPDATE scenario SET name = 'x' on a scenario in Budget Lock, never calling the service's functions. What happens?

options.text: The update is stored, since the service's Python checks were bypassed
options.says: The rule is in the schema too: the raw UPDATE raised 'scenario is locked'.

options.text: The update is refused, by a trigger that fires on a locked row's change
options.says: Right: locked_is_frozen fires on an update of a locked row and raises 'scenario is locked'.

options.text: The update is stored, since the trigger watches the state column alone
options.says: locked_is_frozen fires on an update of any column of a locked row; the name change was refused.

options.text: The update is refused, by the partial unique index on the cycle column
options.says: The refusal's message was the trigger's, 'scenario is locked'; the index limits locked scenarios per cycle.
